title: "Appropriate place for inserting a node" refers to elements, but may include DocumentFragments

labels.name: topic: shadow
labels.description: Relates to shadow trees (as defined in DOM)

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

I'm not sure if I'm understanding this correctly but the spec seems to disagree with itself about what the ["appropriate place for inserting a node" algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#appropriate-place-for-inserting-a-node) returns. That algorithm starts:

> The appropriate place for inserting a node, optionally using a particular override target, is the position in an element returned by running the following steps:

To me this suggests it always returns an Element as the parent. This matches how it's used in a couple of places, for example this, from the `<template>` section of the ["in head" insertion mode](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#parsing-main-inhead) parsing algorithm:

>  6. Let the adjustedInsertionLocation be the [appropriate place for inserting a node](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#appropriate-place-for-inserting-a-node).
> 7. Let intendedParent be the element in which the adjustedInsertionLocation finds itself.

However, in multiple cases it actually returns a location inside a `template` element's contents, which is a DocumentFragment, not an Element. eg, step 3:

> 3. If the adjusted insertion location is inside a [template](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#the-template-element) element, let it instead be inside the [template](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#the-template-element) element's [template contents](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#template-contents), after its last child (if any).

I can think of a few possibilities:
1. The term "element" is just misleading/outdated here and is supposed to include DocumentFragments.
2. It should actually always return an Element as the parent, and "inside the template element's template contents" is not supposed to mean the DocumentFragment somehow.
3. "the element in which the adjustedInsertionLocation finds itself" is supposed to do some extra work to walk upwards to the nearest ancestor Element.

For context: I'm mostly unfamiliar with `<template>` and shadow roots, and am trying to fix bugs in Ladybird's implementation. I figure that even if I just misunderstood that "this is confusing" is still useful feedback.
